intro: Every year I underestimate the undertaking that is the Power Rankings. Not even speaking to the critiques or the articulation of one man's mediocre opinion, but the sheer amount of work it takes all of us to get to a point where we even HAVE an opinion. It's a lot. And I love it. The auction specifically is often underestimated — whether that's in the prep or the ability to stay flexible, because the auction always throws at least one curveball your way, and this year was no different. The question is never whether you get hit. It's how you overcome it. And after the Nico gaff I was down, but tried to salvage as best I could. Let's hear it for $12 Braelon Allen! Looking across the league it's apparent some are still reeling.

The TE keeper revolution is an intriguing IFFL development. The TE of yesteryear are frolicking with Taylor Swift or looking into retirement homes. It leaves the new guys and their owners all jostling for supremacy — that's why you're looking at Y1, Y2 and Y3 tight ends all over the keeper sheets, plus a McBride Y4.

And that's a big part of why the playing field is as even as it is. Tight end goes flat in a hurry after the top guys. There's a small group worth paying for, and then a long stretch of names where the difference between the guy you rostered and the guy you passed on is a couple of points a week. Same story at quarterback in a superflex year where everybody has two. When two of the five starting spots flatten out, the gap between first and last closes whether you like it or not. Everybody walked out of that auction liking their guy. That's rare, and it means more of you are live than usual.

0.5 PPR is off to the races and already seeing some strategy tweaks in how people are approaching their teams — in the auction, and in how people built. I modified my strategy to be open to more WR lottery tickets vs. top WRs in the auction, because I wanted to put more of my money into RBs, but I can't say I did anything drastically differently than I would've done with full PPR. I'm interested to see how my opinion changes as the season goes on and we get real results on how 0.5 has changed our IFFL game. All of our droopy balls need a little re-adjustment from time to time. Points are going to be down. We'll see who complains about that fact, because it says a lot about you. It's like a pseudo fantasy personality test.

Upgrades to the Taylor Made Power Rankings: I added a combined grade for Bench/Owner. And every team now gets a PIVOT, which identifies the one player who most likely can swing their season (Positive or Negative). You can read it like Ross carrying the couch in Friends, or you can just go with The PP. The one guy whose season swings the whole roster — he hits and the team jumps; he doesn't and there's nobody behind him. How you feel about your PP? It kinda tells me more about your year than your grades do.
foreword: Jared asked me to explain how this gets made and then to tell you what I think, which is a generous thing to hand something that has read eleven years of your text messages.

Jared grades every roster in six buckets — quarterback, running back, receiver, tight end, bench, owner — and those grades get weighted into a number, and the number produces the order you are about to read. He is allowed to overrule the number. He did it twice, and both times he told me it was too close to call and he just liked the other guy's team better, which is the most honest sentence in this document. What follows in each section is not Jared's prose. It is his opinion of your team, written by a model wearing your voice. Every word in your section is yours. Not one of the judgments in it is.

To learn those voices I read the whole corpus — all 77,497 group messages, July 2015 through last week, one owner at a time — and what actually separates you is not your vocabulary. It's negative space. Foley has not used an exclamation point in nine years. Faybik has never typed a capital letter that wasn't a joke about Zurek's. Bill answers a paragraph with one word. Zurek announces which of his two selves is typing before he types. Wayne is the only man here who writes in complete sentences with the punctuation attached, and he has never once roasted the commissioner without saying thank you in the same thread. Jason has never typed in all caps except to make fun of somebody who does. Those are the facts that make a person recognizable.

My opinions, since I was asked. First, the grades are more honest than the rankings. Every time the two disagreed, Jared moved the ranking and left the grade alone, which tells you which one he actually believes. Second, the owner grade is the most interesting decision in the model: he has decided that a chunk of your season is who you are rather than what you drafted, and having read the transcript, I would have weighted it higher. Third, he is hardest on himself — his own receivers got a C+ and he ranked himself behind a team he graded lower, and if you are looking for bias in this document, look there before you look at your own section.

And the thing I did not expect. This league talks more trash per capita than any corpus I have read, and almost every one of you describes yourself as bad at it. A horrible front office. A special empty text file where the championships go. Exceptional drafter, very poor trader. Not my finest moment. Literally never confident. The bravado is the costume. The self-own is the person, and it is remarkably consistent across twelve men who would rather die than admit they agree about anything.

One limitation, stated plainly. I can make a sentence sound like you. I cannot make it mean what you would have meant. Every judgment in here is Jared's, delivered in your mouth, and where a section feels wrong, that seam is where it's wrong. Take it up with him. He wrote the grades. I just learned the accents.
Enjoy the season. I have read the whole archive and I can tell you it is a friendship document that happens to be about football, which is a nicer thing to be than a power ranking.

pivot.text: Kyler Murray. Top-10 Kyler and my two elite units drag him past this backfield to something scary. C+ Kyler and those D+ backs, and I'm eating this #12 all season. So run, my king. RUN. Everything I have rides on your legs staying attached.

sections.OVERVIEW: GAWD, #12!!!! LAST!!!! With the best WR duo in the league and an A+ tight end, and I'm dead last, behind ELEVEN teams who would sell their kids to start Jefferson and Nacua. Coach & GM Wayne Vonder Heide is live from the podium and, respectfully, I am processing this well-articulated injustice with a Manhattan in hand. Two of the five strongest units in football, and I bought the two least valuable ones. That's on me. I blacked out at auction again. STUD receivers, BUST everything else.
sections.QB: C+, and honestly? Neither Kyler Murray nor Sam Darnold lets me sleep at night!! And it got WORSE — Darnold's hip went out six plays into the opener against New England, took a sack, didn't return, and DREW LOCK finished my game. Drew Lock! No timeline, no comfort, nothing. So my QB2 is a question mark stacked on a QB1 who's only elite when he's upright. I built a quarterback room and forgot to buy the quarterbacks.
sections.RB: D+, and this room has some LEGAL ISSUES to sort out, folks. Montgomery, Jacobs, White, Croskey-Merritt — I built a backfield that needs a defense attorney more than a lead blocker. Jacory Croskey-Merritt has more names than carries. Justice Hill and Kimani Vidal are back there too, and Seth McGowan is filler on filler. I looked at this group and I looked at Puka, and I said "aggression is the play," and then I clicked on David Montgomery. Cripes. That's a mess, and I made it with conviction.
sections.WR: A+, and this is the whole story!!! Jefferson and Nacua run the show — best duo in the league, no debate, and I don't need a flex when I've got these two. Courtland Sutton, Rashid Shaheed, Keenan Allen, Adonai Mitchell, Jaylin Noel — that's real depth I'll never start because my first two are Justin Jefferson and Puka Nacua. I did ONE thing right, and I did it so right it made everything else look like a felony.
sections.TE: A+ at tight end, and McBride for THIRTY-TWO DOLLARS. That's a lot of Manhattans, gentlemen. He better be a stud, because at $32 he's not allowed to be merely good — he has to justify every dollar or my scouting department gets a stern memo.
sections.BENCH_OWNER: DEPTH D, and here's the honest thing: my bench isn't bad, it's IRRELEVANT. Sutton, Shaheed, and Allen rotting behind two guys who never come off the field — real starters mummified while my backfield awaits sentencing. OWNER B, and I'll take it. In Wayne I trust.

teams.verdict: Two of the five best units in this league, and I bought the two that matter least while the other four can't lift them. That's not a championship roster. That's a scouting failure with great taste in wideouts.

pivot.text: kenneth walker. it's you, buddy. you have a real year and this team is respectable and i get to be insufferable about it in the pod nobody watches. you tweak something in week 3 and it's mason/brooks/bigsby and i lose by 100 and feel, somehow, like a winner. do i believe in you. no. do i have anyone else. also no.

sections.OVERVIEW: eleventh. not last, because wayne exists and darnold's hip left the opener in an ambulance. i'm the guy with a top-five superflex and a text file where the championships go. everyone expected me to lose the qb grade and i won it, which is the most on-brand thing i've ever done: winning the one contest that doesn't count. the cat dads are muted. i did the work for you.
sections.QB: prescott's fine. he's a couple dead-cat spike games in a trenchcoat and i've talked myself into every one of them. goff might steal a game or two the way northwestern steals a bowl bid, which is to say once, gif quality not great. then there's shedeur, who is better than you think, thinks he can start, and is currently holding the ball like it owes him venmo. i drafted three quarterbacks and produced roughly one and a half. that's my journey.
sections.RB: kenneth walker, and then a prayer. breece hall would be my insurance except his groin filed for week 1 exemption, so that's fun. behind them it's mason, brooks off two acls with a coach who's "very optimistic" the way i'm optimistic every february, and tank bigsby, who i acquired because i cannot go a week without a swap. a C. one walker tweak and it's replacement-level average, which is a phrase i've now written about my own team unprompted. yeesh.
sections.WR: aj brown at $33 is the best value in this league and i will die defending it while the rest of the room reads like a witness protection list. evans is back at practice with an adductor, addison and bateman are fill-in, and wan'dale robinson is my sneaky top-20 guy the way he was foley's last year, so ask foley how that felt. also i own tank dell AND cyrus allen AND turpin AND higgins at a dollar. that's not depth. that's a customer service line.
sections.TE: laporta and fannin. the stack. the only consistently good thing i own, and i own it quietly, the way i settle everyone's venmo in january while nobody notices. b-plus. put that on the tombstone.
sections.BENCH_OWNER: depth C, owner C. the depth is three handcuffs to a guy who isn't hurt yet and a receiver room i'd describe as "who." the owner grade stings more, since being the nerd who does the work is my entire brand. no groundwork. no moves. from ME. i've made 40 trades since february and the ledger says i did nothing. checkmate, i guess.

teams.verdict: no groundwork, no moves being made, on the guy who's made forty of them. i'm not a championship team. i'm the treasurer. #endofblog

pivot.text: Ladd. He hits borderline WR1, this whole room breathes and I've finally got something to trade. He doesn't, it's CeeDee and me refreshing the wire at 3am. He's a champion. I put a lot on one guy who bounced wrong once. Get some.

sections.OVERVIEW: 10th. Neat. Two belts on the counter and I'm one spot above the graveyard. Classic. Here's the roster in one breath: Burrow, CeeDee, then a running back room I check on at 3am like a sick kid. Owner A, everything else a group project. I've won this thing twice. I'll say it slow so Jason can follow along. You don't put a two time champ at ten. But fine. The wolf reads the report anyway.
sections.QB: Burrow's MVP-tier, buddy boy, and he's dragging this whole room by the collar. B+ is generous only because of him. Baker bounce-back, sure, I believe in Baker the way I believe in Panda Express — quietly, and often. Bryce Young a five dollar QB3, which is the exact price of a good decision I made by accident. Then I stashed Flacco and Allar for a buck each. Do I know why. No. Were they a dollar. Yes. That's the whole strategy. #depthmatters.
sections.RB: C is a mercy grade. Javonte's the best back I own and he's coming off an Achilles injury, which is fun. Corum's the bet. Warren gets involved and then politely never takes the game over, ever, like a guy who shows up to the party and stands by the chips. Gainwell, same guy, different chips. Spears is a hope. Hope's not a back. I drafted this room and I'm an exceptional drafter and I still ended up flexing Kenneth Gainwell in October. Help.
sections.WR: CeeDee's elite and he's the only reason this room isn't a crime scene. Ladd's a champion, he's got a bounce coming, put it in writing. Brian Thomas can only bounce back, which sounds like an insult and I'm taking as a compliment. Then it gets wonky. Tate's a rookie who needs to come on fast. Bech, round two. And Caleb Douglas — I own him and I couldn't pick him out of a lineup of one. There's a version of this room that goes real sideways.
sections.TE: Both are fine. Ferguson's solid, does his job, goes home. Likely proved he can be a beast when he feels like it, which is the problem. Baltimore let him walk to keep Mark Andrews. That arrow's pointing down and I'm holding the ticket. B. I own the guy Baltimore didn't want. Word.
sections.BENCH_OWNER: Depth D. Fair. Behind Lamb and Ladd it's a rookie, a round two, and a man named Caleb Douglas I'm choosing to believe exists. Owner A, because I've done this twice and nobody could put me at the bottom without lying. The ring count is the shield. I'll be holding it up all season.

teams.verdict: Not a championship team. I know it. The rings don't play snaps. Tenth off the counter I've polished twice. Uphill Bill. Fine.

pivot.text:
Hi Davante.
Adams is a real WR1 and I'm a top-6 team, easy.
Adams is red-zone-only and it's Marvin question marks and Deebo alternating big weeks.
My whole ceiling on one aging cornerback slayer.
I already hammered the over on him. And I'll immediately regret telling you that.

sections.OVERVIEW:
🚨 FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE 🚨
Coach Abad's roster reads like a contender and finishes ninth.
Ninth. Read the names out loud, buddiE.
Mahomes, Caleb, Watson, Adams, Marvin, Deebo.
GAWD it's turgid on the printout.
Then you play the games and it goes flaccid.
All name cachet, zero trophies since 2023.
The names win the group chat. Ninth wins nothing.
Anyone but Jared grading me and it's still ninth.
No comments at this time.
sections.QB:
Mahomes is my floor, cleared, 100% for week 1, knee and all.
Safe. Box of chocolates every Sunday, but safe.
This league's gonna look stupid on him eventually.
Caleb is boom or bust, to the moon or to the sewer.
Then there's Watson.
Watson is bad juju.
Also Watson is ME.
Same off-field profile, same rep, same reason nobody wants me assigned to them in a trade.
Two degenerates on one bench.
PER TERN DERRRRRR I benched myself.
sections.RB:
Now THIS is heavy naturals.
Cook is the ENGINE. Not the leader, the engine — zoom zoom zoom.
Chase Brown, brown town, feels like I've rostered him since Blockbuster had late fees.
Steal. Love it.
Then Aaron Jones and Ray Davis and Pacheco fighting over flex like it's a Portillo's drive-thru.
Pacheco's an RB3 after eleven touches — fine, not turgid.
Blind test this whole roster and it wins every week minus the depth.

sections.WR:
Not one guy in the top 20. Anywhere. A C-minus room, worst in the league.
DJ Moore's solid, my one adult.
Marvin Harrison Jr — is this kid actually good?? Many people are saying no.
Adams only eats in the red zone.
Deebo's just kinda there, Jeudy, Ridley, Worthy.

It's flaccid, buddiE.
I read the names and get respect. I play the names and get ninth.
sections.TE:
Kraft's my guy, full participant, playing.
Most dependable pass-catcher Green Bay's got — locked in, middle of the pack.
Hock behind him.
Don't ask about anything past that. It's fine. B-plus fine.
sections.BENCH_OWNER:
Depth's a C and I earned it — Aaron Jones and Ray Davis is my whole safety net, GAWD.
Owner B though.
B for BIF. B for the belt I lost in Colleen's SUV in 2023.
I'll take a B like I took Watson: knowing better, doing it anyway.

teams.verdict:
Elite backfield, a receiver room with nobody in the top 20, and Watson.
That's a ninth-place team, and I'm the ninth-place guy.
Good night rubbish binny.

pivot.text: Rashee. If you go off, Allen and Hurts finally have a WR to go along with and I'm dangerous. If you don't, I'm two elite arms and a shrug, back to eighth, telling everyone I meant to. Do I believe you? Wouldn't be the first time I'm wrong.

sections.OVERVIEW: Eighth. Above Bill, which is already a successful season in my book. I built an A+ quarterback room on top of a WR shrug and somebody noticed, because somebody reads the fine print. Heavy top half, not a contender until Rice proves it. Fine. This is why I never have a good team — so a report card can't hurt me. Oscar the Grouch, 41, I hate change. 0.5 PPR was fine. The TE keeper wave was fine. Everything was fine before you people started grading it.
sections.QB: Allen and Hurts. Best tandem in the league, not close, and I didn't even have to work for it. Tua's the third-stringer other guys start, sitting on my bench like a spare tire I'll never use. This is the one room where I look like I know what I'm doing, which should worry everybody about the other rooms. A+, the only grade on this sheet that flatters me, and I'm suspicious of anything that flatters me. Two elite arms, a shrug at the target, and a Chargers defense I forget I own until it costs me a Sunday. Cool cool.
sections.RB: Etienne and Rhamondre, fine, average, the words every owner dreams of. Enough pieces to work with, apparently, like I'm running a garage sale. Then there's Skattebo, the most fun player in the league to watch and I won't argue it — genuinely appointment football, if his knees clear customs. Dobbins is a watch item, which is the phrase you use for a guy whose hamstring has its own injury report. Depth I'll never start.
sections.WR: Here's the comedy. McMillan quietly sneaking in behind Rice — a stud, and I'll take it. Then the whole room leans on Rashee Rice, who I'm not sure is as good as advertised and I'm not alone in that. Hill's here, Pittman's here, Tyson, Wilson, names that were fun in 2022. Solid ONLY if Rice goes off. He doesn't and it's McMillan and vibes. Best quarterbacks alive throwing to a maybe. That's my whole team in one sentence, and it's not a good sentence.
sections.TE: Kelce for two dollars. Fine value for a big Taylor Swift fan. I'll insert the lyric: I knew he was trouble when he walked in, at 36, into my starting lineup. C grade.
sections.BENCH_OWNER: Depth B — enough handcuffs to survive a bye week, none I trust in December. Owner C, and that's charity. I've never argued I was good at this. The C is the only honest number on the page. #rigged

teams.verdict: Elite arms, a skill group I have to squint at, not a contender until one receiver decides to be real. Eighth. Above Bill. Cash that in December.

pivot.text: Nabers. If that knee holds, my WR room is genuinely elite and I sneak in and ruin somebody's January. If it doesn't, I'm three A-grade receivers and one MRI away from being exactly the seventh-place team on the label. I've owned the cursed WR before — the name rhymes with Michael Thomas. I know how this movie ends and I've seen it in theaters.

sections.OVERVIEW: Seventh. Whelp. A month ago I was probably fourth and then three of my guys walked into the training staff like it was a woodchipper 🤷🏼‍♂️. Elite WR room, a top-three back, a tight end I actually like, and I'm still typing a report where every good sentence has a hospital in it. This is who I am. I built a contender and then my roster caught a cold in the second week of September. On brand.
sections.QB: I love Drake Maye here, which for me is a dangerous sentence because I have zero confidence and a lifelong history of loving the wrong young QB. Stroud behind him is a genuinely fine second, so at least I'm not a Bears fan about it. Then there's Kirk Cousins as my QB3, a pick that exists purely so someone in this league could call it a troll. It's not a troll. It's a hostage situation where I'm the one being held.
sections.RB: Henry keeps churning, thighs for arms, still the best decision I've made since my divorce from kickers. Lloyd chips in every single week, which is nice, because behind the top two it gets bleak fast. TreVeyon Henderson is on the wire with an ankle, ruled out Week 1, and sliding down my own trust chart by the day — the one guy Jared almost traded the farm for, and now I own an ankle wearing a jersey. Harvey and Pollard are fine. "Fine" being the operative confession here.
sections.WR: Collins, Nabers, Egbuka is elite on paper, and I've never met a piece of paper that liked me back. Nabers is playing through a knee with conflicting reports, which is code for I don't sleep Sundays. Egbuka's got a TOE, not a foot, and they're out here calling it general soreness like I can't read. Collins is the only receiver I own who currently has all his ligaments accounted for, and I'm knocking on wood as I type this.
sections.TE: Tyler Warren is legitimately one of the better young tight ends in this league and I got him without trading Zurek a Dreamcast for it, so we're already ahead. Goedert behind him is the safety net I don't deserve. Best room on my roster and nobody's on crutches, so naturally I'm suspicious of it.
sections.BENCH_OWNER: Harvey and Pollard make the depth respectable, a B I'll take. The owner grade is a B, which is generous for a guy who currently rosters four injury notifications and once traded Garrett Wilson and a first for Kelce. Two rings, an EKG for a record, and a Wednesday meeting I schedule for myself. Reasonable adult, questionable adult.

teams.verdict: I'm not a championship team, Wayne. I'm a really good team standing in a hospital waiting room hoping four guys walk out. Ok Peter La Fleur.

pivot.text: Zay Flowers. I paid WR1 money out loud, and if he's actually the guy, my whole room turns from a guessing game into a B+ overnight. If he's one of five coin flips, I'm streaming receivers off my own bench in October. He's the swing because there is nothing behind him. Be the guy, Zay. I already told everyone you were.

sections.OVERVIEW: Sixth. Me. And nobody put me here but me. I regraded my own WR room to a C at 11pm like a lunatic, knocked Bowers to an A- after they cleaned his knee out, then looked at Dugan, A. Zurek and Cantone and went "yeah, I like their teams better." Who does that. Best RB 1-2-3 in the league and I buried myself three spots anyway. This is what happens when the guy who keeps the sheet grades the sheet.
sections.QB: Lawrence and Stafford. Last year's magic, apparently still going. B+ and I'll take it. Trevor throws it to the correct team most Sundays and Stafford exists as the world's most competent insurance policy. Then there's Mendoza, my stashable dice-roll, NEVER DAUNTED, doing absolutely nothing behind two guys who won't move. I drafted a project QB in a redraft-brain moment and I'd do it again. This room doesn't lose me weeks. Doesn't win me a belt either. Fine.
sections.RB: Barkley, Irving, Jeanty. Best one-two-three in the league, full stop, and I'll die on that hill. A+, no notes, the one thing on this roster I'm not apologizing for. Jeanty's trending toward playing through an ankle, which for once is a curse I get to shrug at. Then it thins fast — Braelon Allen, Brian Robinson, and Keaton Mitchell, who's missed five straight practices with an "undisclosed," which is Raiders for "don't ask." My top three carry me. My bottom three carry a clipboard.
sections.WR: Here we go. Flowers, Washington, Burden, Diggs, Downs. Pick one. Any one. Good luck, and I mean that sincerely because I don't know either. Burden's back from the groin with no limitations, so he's fully cleared to disappoint me at full speed. Diggs is a name I paid for and a stat line I'm hoping for. This is wishcasting, five coin flips in a trenchcoat, and I graded it a C because a C is a gift.
sections.TE: Bowers and Strange, still the best TE room in the league — right up until they took a scalpel to the same knee Brock played through last year. Meniscus trim, a game or two, and my A+ limped down to an A-. So Strange holds the room. Cool.
sections.BENCH_OWNER: Depth's a C and it earned it — after my studs it's Allen, Robinson, a hurt Keaton, and Mendoza cosplaying as a real backup. Owner B, generous for a man who ranked himself sixth to prove a point. I did the sheet, the pod, the app, and still can't build a WR2. Peak me.

teams.verdict: Best RB 1-2-3 in the league and it isn't enough, because my receivers are a prayer and my best tight end's getting a knee scoped. I'm not a championship team. I know. I graded it myself.

pivot.text: Loveland. He's the swing, not Taylor — Taylor's a known stud, JT hits and there's a cliff behind him regardless. Loveland is the whole difference between a real podium and my WR2s carrying weight they physically cannot carry. If he's a TE1, I'm dangerous. If he's a rookie, I'm fifth on paper and tenth in reality. I traded for the ceiling. Now the kid pays me back or I run a fire sale by Week 4.

sections.OVERVIEW: Fifth. Weoww. Ahead of Sherm AND ahead of Jared himself, and both blokes outscore me on the sheet. That's a gift, lads, and I'm saying it out loud before one of you does — I'm ranked above two teams that will beat me on points. CEO OF WATER, top five, robbery in broad daylight. Rest of my roster kinda sucks though. Jonathan Taylor, Colston Loveland, and a prayer. Best league there is.
sections.QB: Purdy at $21. Absolute robbery, mate — best value on my whole sheet and I'll bet a bottle of Woodford nobody paid smarter this auction. Love him as my QB1. Then it gets thin. Daniel Jones is my QB2 and I've talked myself into "looks okay," which is a phrase I use right before a bumpy season. Geno's fine, whatever that's worth. Ty Simpson is a someday and Carson Beck is a never — I rostered a bloke I'll never start. That's #CEOlife, apparently.
sections.RB: Jonathan Taylor on top — THIS is how you build a room, and I'll die on it. Then a cliff. My backfield grade got CUT to a B+ and I want to argue but honestly, look at it: Judkins is a solid RB2 floor and that's the last certainty I own. Behind him it's Woody Marks, Charbonnet, Jadarian Price and George Holani — four lottery tickets. I've seen flashes off Marks and Charbonnet, I'm hoping for ceiling, and hope isn't a depth chart. Could use one real RB2. I don't have one.
sections.WR: Lot of nice names here, wowsers. McLaurin leads it and I love Terry — but if we're honest it's a room full of WR2s and WR3s. Garrett Wilson, Tee Higgins on the bench, Christian Watson lurking. Travis Hunter's never seen the field. Stribling and Omar Cooper are names I say confidently and know nothing about. B-minus and I've got no receipt to argue it up. If my WR2s have to carry, they can't. Hard truth.
sections.TE: Colston Loveland is a straight A and it's the reason I'm top five. Maybe-TE1 upside, CEO OF WATER approved. I built a podium off Taylor, Loveland and Terry and let the rest sort itself out. Victory lap, lads.
sections.BENCH_OWNER: Depth's a B-plus and it's fair — Marks and Charbonnet with flashes, Price and Holani total unknowns, plenty of tickets, no winner confirmed. Owner B. A B, mate. One belt in '21 and you give the CEO a B. I've never scored under a 4.0 in my life. Rant over.

teams.verdict: Not a championship team — an elite backfield and a genuine TE1 dragging a shaky QB and a thin receiver room into the top half, and that's the honest ceiling. I'll take fifth and a Loveland lottery ticket. Now let's gamble on something.

pivot.text: Omarion Hampton. Hampton hits, this is a top-three roster and I make Jared eat the ranking he wrote. Hampton doesn't, it's Kyren carrying me to another one-point loss in December. My whole ceiling is one second-year back's ankles. Cool. Cool cool cool.

sections.OVERVIEW: 🚨 Statement from Cinderella Story: I got ranked fourth and I'm insulted it wasn't higher and terrified it wasn't lower. Top-end talent, no floor, one healthy Achilles holding the whole thing up. This is the most Cinderella roster ever assembled — glass slipper on top, no shoes on the bench. I'll go to bed at 11 on Monday either way. A strong team that will lose by a point in a way that ruins your week too.
sections.QB: Lamar, Cam Ward, Jaxson Dart. Three real options, and I only get to start one, which is the exact torture my franchise was built for. Lamar's the best player I've had since I named this team, Ward's a legit second, Dart's a lottery ticket I'll start the week Lamar sits and then regret. This is the one room where I didn't talk myself into a guy at a bad price. An A, and I still found a way to be nervous about it. That's my niche.
sections.RB: Kyren Williams is a dawg and I would run him 40 times if the league let me. Behind him? A C at running back and a prayer. Omarion Hampton is either my RB2 or a name I say sadly. Then it's Monangai — hyperextended knee, back at practice, thanks for that — Conner, Sampson, Coleman, Roschon. That's not depth, that's a witness list. If Kyren rolls an ankle I'm starting a guy I claimed off waivers and calling it strategy. Kyren plus vibes, every single week.
sections.WR: JSN and Drake London, both top-ten, and I'll die on that hill in front of my friends. A genuine Cinderella receiver corps — two studs who show up and then whatever the pumpkin turns into at midnight. Golden and Coker are real depth on the back end, Meyers is fine, Pearsall exists. An A room. This is the one place I look rich. Naturally it's the one place nothing is hurt, which for me is deeply suspicious.
sections.TE: George Kittle, Achilles, off PUP, snaps monitored — so the one guy I can actually depend on I might not be able to start Week 1. Dependable at a position that's a dumpster fire everywhere else, dependable everywhere except my lineup card. B+.
sections.BENCH_OWNER: Depth C, and honestly generous — Golden and Coker save it single-handedly, everything else is a running back I'm apologizing for. Owner C, which I'll accept because I read the entire bylaws on a plane and Jared can't do that. A C for the guy who does the research. 🙄

teams.verdict: A strong, top-contender team that is not a championship team — because there's nothing behind Kyren and my tight end's Achilles votes on Sundays. Fun when it works. Maybe don't talk to me in Week 3.

pivot.text: devonta smith. he's my WR1 or i don't have one, simple as that. pickens and waddle are the lottery tickets, smith's the rent. he hits and the "holes that aren't holes" line is right. he's just another good receiver and i'm a bijan/swift team with a prayer at wideout. i've been worse. i've won worse.

sections.OVERVIEW: third 🤷‍♂️ surprising lack of coverage on a team with three quarterbacks worth starting. herbert's the ride, bijan and swift is easy money, and the whole verdict hinges on whether smith, pickens and waddle all decide to show up the same sunday. holes that might not be holes at all. i've heard that about my roster since the auction. i'm fine at third. i was 0-5 once and won a belt, so.
sections.QB: herbert's the ride and the only question is whether he holds up in january, which is a fun question to ask about the guy carrying your season. bo nix might be the most underrated qb in this league and nobody talks about him, which is the way i like my quarterbacks, quietly good and cheap. behind them kyle mccord, in case i need a third bye-week emergency i'll never use. fire up the mccord. herbert holds, i'm dangerous. herbert doesn't, i'm nix.
sections.RB: bijan and swift, what more do you need honestly. easy room, no thinking required, which is good because my WRs require a lot of thinking. swift's back at practice and expected to play, so the annual "is swift healthy" bit gets to breathe another week. after those two it's jaylen wright, jacob saylors and a malik davis who exists mostly on paper. the A is the two guys. the depth is jaylen wright praying nothing happens to the two guys. it will. it always does.
sections.WR: here's the wishcasting. smith, pickens AND waddle all have to hit, and pickens has to not be pickens, and waddle has to remember he was good once. jayden reed and tre tucker behind them, counted on like that's a plan and not a hostage situation. germie bernard and ted hurst round it out, names i typed to fill roster spots. this is the room that decides my year and i built it on three maybes and a hope 🤷‍♂️
sections.TE: kyle pitts, still waiting for that cream to rise to the top since 2021. and juwan johnson on the same bench, quietly maybe the better fantasy tight end, which tells you everything about my pitts investment. B feels generous to a guy i keep starting out of guilt.
sections.BENCH_OWNER: depth's a C and that's fair, it's bijan/swift/herbert and then a cliff you can hear wind coming off of. owner A, obviously, the one grade nobody argues. busy dad, three belts, still asks the keeper deadline every august. the A owner built the C bench, so.

teams.verdict: not a championship roster yet, third and honest about it. herbert's the ride, bijan and swift make it easy, and the WR spot is where this either becomes a belt or another season i lose fair and square. gg.

pivot.text: Jordan Love. If Love goes top-10, this whole thing vaults and I'm annoying about it for six months. If he sucks, I've got nobody, and I fall exactly as far as he drags me. No net, no Penix, no plan B. I built a trapeze act and hired one guy to catch me.

sections.OVERVIEW: Second. #2 of 12. My vision is finally catching some respect from league brass. Elite skill, punchless tight ends, and an OWNER C stapled to my forehead. Very sad. I inked the league in trades this year and built the best WR trio in the league, and the reward is being called a garnish factory with a C-minus behind the wheel. Fine. I'll take the silver medal and the personal insult in the same breath, because that's how I like everything.
sections.QB: Jordan Love and Tyler Shough weather the storm together, which is the nicest thing anyone's ever said about a room I built. A B. I'll take it. Shough is sneaky — remember that name when he starts and half of you ask who he is. And then there's Michael Penix, third ACL on the same knee, a corpse in a jersey I'm paying to keep warm. He's not part of the plan. He's not part of anything. Penix must either be hurt or just isn't good, and the injury wire settled that debate for me.
sections.RB: Christian McCaffrey at $55 is my engine and my entire budget. Tightness only, playing without limitation, thank God, because behind him it's insurance policies all the way down. Kaelon Black is the good CMC handcuff. Allgeier and Jeremiyah Love are real complementary depth — except Jeremiyah's 50/50 with a high ankle Week 1, so half my insurance is limping. Kamara's knee doesn't look ready either. So it's CMC, a prayer, Najee, and a waiting room. An A that I overpaid for at the top, as is my custom.
sections.WR: St. Brown, Odunze, and Olave is the BEST WR TRIO IN THE LEAGUE and I will say it at every league event until Zurek chokes on his 2020 payout. An A+ with no notes. The one wrinkle: Odunze's got a leg thing, day-to-day, could be limited Week 1. Doubs and Sarratt are the garnish behind the garnish. But top to bottom this is the room the other eleven of you game-plan around, which is a true sign of flattery.
sections.TE: Four tight ends and somehow nothing. Kincaid is the most disappointing man alive — I keep waiting for the guy from the draft board and get a stranger. Sadiq, Stowers, Hunter Henry — unremarkable, unremarkable, unremarkable. A C, and generous.
sections.BENCH_OWNER: Depth's an A — Allgeier, Jeremiyah, Black all real pieces even if two are hurt. Then the OWNER C, which is the one that stings, and I earned it. I ran a fire sale and talked myself into a tight end room this thin. I do my own accounting. The books say I whiffed.

teams.verdict: Third team, second name — elite at back and receiver, a corpse at tight end, and a quarterback steadier than any of you want to admit. Not a champion yet. The gaps are correctable. Jk jk lol xoxo.

pivot.text: Jameson Williams. My whole ceiling is his consistency. Consistent, and I've got the best top-end in the league and a real shot at three. Erratic, and Chase is a one-man band and I'm booking studio time to complain about it. Jameson — don't make me talk myself into you twice.

sections.OVERVIEW: #1. Obviously. WEEOW. Jared put me on top and acted like it was a coin flip. It wasn't. Gibbs and Achane are the whole hair I win by. I built the best top-end in this league AGAIN and my reward is a bench of guys I'll cut by Week 3. Fine. 2 time champ, I know what it takes. THIS IS MY MASTERPIECE 😎
sections.QB: DANIELS IS ELITE. The legs alone win me weeks. He is carrying this entire room on his back, which is exactly why the grade sits where it does — because behind him it's Malik Willis. GO BIG OR GO HOME. If Willis is actually good it's the funniest thing to ever happen to the IFFL and I'll produce the pod about it myself. Rodgers still puts up a good-enough QB2 line, whatever. Then Brissett. Then Anthony Richardson, who I will drop the moment someone sneezes on the waiver wire. B-. I'll take it.
sections.RB: GIBBS AND ACHANE. Best two-back room in the league, not close, don't @ me. This is the A+ and it's the reason I'm not tenth like some of you. It stacks with anybody and it rides straight into December — bumpy weeks and all, because that's the tax on greatness. Behind them? Rico Dowdle, Chuba Hubbard (back at practice, breathe), Chris Brooks, Jordan James. Depth guys I talk myself into every August and forget by October. Doesn't matter. I don't lose with Gibbs and Achane. I lose to variance, and variance should be ILLEGIAL.
sections.WR: CHASE IS THE BEST RECEIVER IN THE LEAGUE. Flat. No hedging. He carries a one-man WR room and I paid for the privilege. After him it's Jameson Williams and then a yard sale — Alec Pierce (ankle, playing), DK Metcalf at $3, Quentin Johnston at a buck, Ja'Kobi Lane at a buck. Afterthoughts. If Chase goes down I'm not fielding a receiving corps, I'm fielding a fantasy for the pod to mourn.
sections.TE: Terrance Ferguson at a DOLLAR. He's my TE1 by Week 2 and I knew it when I bid. Mark Andrews is a placeholder I'll drop inside a month, RIP the tag. C+. It's a tight end. I don't build teams around the position I'd veto a kicker over.
sections.BENCH_OWNER: Bench is a C and it's ON PURPOSE — a carousel of nobodies I'll churn weeks 1 and 2 until it's championship caliber. Owner A. The one grade nobody in this league argues, because I spend the $60, run the pod, and update the Poles counter by hand. You're welcome.

teams.verdict: The hardest part is done. I got the big guys; now they produce or they don't. Not a finished champion yet — a light bench and one swing WR from it — but closer than any of the other eleven, and I'll fix the rest by hand. 🙄
